title: connection-keystone-and-soft-fallback-broker-for-tactical-regional-drain-hotfix
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce lightweight connection lease coordinator (connection-keystone) and a soft-fallback broker to reduce SLO violations during regional drain windows. Mitigates double-release causing circuit flapping; safe rollout to 10% canary then full rollout.
description: Context and motivation: After the 2025-01-02 partial regional degradation incident (SUP-5012) we observed repeated circuit flips and a spike in tail latency when draining nodes during regional failovers. Root cause analysis pointed to two compounding issues: (1) in-flight connection state was being released too early during staged drains causing duplicated KV-cache eviction and transient cache misses, and (2) our fallback path aggressively reconnected traffic which created request bursts and tripped SLO circuits. This PR introduces a lightweight 'connection-keystone' lease coordinator and a 'soft-fallback-broker' to smooth the transition during tactical regional drains. Summary of changes: - Add connection-keystone: a lease that pins in-flight connections for a short grace period during node drain; coordinates with KV-preserve to avoid premature cache eviction. - Add soft-fallback-broker: on detected capacity perturbation, broker routes a configurable fraction of degraded requests to standby variants or a dedicated soft capacity pool and injects jittered backoff to prevent fan-out bursts. - Fix double-release bug in drain path (race in connection teardown + KV-preserve) that could cause circuit instability. - Canary rollout manifest and a new e2e test harness to simulate staggered drain + failover. Checklist: - [x] Design review with SRE and Runtime (ENG-2147) - [x] Unit tests for lease behavior - [x] e2e simulation reproducing prior failure pattern - [x] Canary deploy to eu-west-1 (10%) - [x] Observability: add metrics and traces - [x] Release notes and rollback plan Commits (high-level): - commit 1: runtime: introduce connection-keystone lease coordinator (keystone.go) - commit 2: fallback: implement soft-fallback-broker and routing policy (broker.go) - commit 3: fix: race in drain teardown and add KV-preserve handshake - commit 4: tests: unit + e2e harness + canary manifest Changes / files touched (high level): - runtime/connection/keystone.go (new): lease coordinator, public API AcquireLease/ReleaseLease - runtime/fallback/broker.go (new): broker with weighted routing and jittered backoff - controlplane/drain/keystone_handshake.go (mod): handshake between drain controller and keystone - controlplane/manifests/canary/eu-west-1-canary.yaml (new): 10% canary manifest - tests/e2e/drain_simulation/soft_fallback_scenario_test.go (new): harness + validation - docs/operational/keystone.md (new): operator runbook + rollback steps Small illustrative snippet (conceptual, not full diff): AcquireLease(connectionID) -> returns leaseToken; on drain, drain controller calls PreserveKV(leaseToken) before connection teardown so KV isn't evicted review conversation: - Tomás Rivera: "Can you quantify the extra memory/descriptor overhead for holding leases?" Asha: "Per-lease overhead is ~120 bytes + map entry; worst-case 5k leases/zone adds ~600KB + GC pressure which we mitigated by TTL-based fast-expiry; numbers included in ENG-2147 design doc." - Meera Shah: "Soft-fallback broker timing looks good but we need a safety cap to avoid starving fastpath; please add a hard ceiling to routed % per tenant." Asha: "Added tenant-level hard cap (default 20%) and made it configurable via feature flag." - Liam O'Connor: "I saw a flaky unit test earlier, did CI clean up?" Asha: "CI failed on first run due to a timing-based test assert; I adjusted harness to use testclock and re-ran. See CI log below." CI summary: - initial run: 1 failing test in TestLeaseExpiry (timing flake) - rerun: all checks passed (unit, integration, linters, e2e-sim) Observability and metrics added: - keystone.leases.active (gauge) - keystone.leases.grace_taken (counter) - fallback.broker.routed_fraction (histogram) - trace spans: keystone.acquire / keystone.release / fallback.route Decision and rollout: - Canary 10% eu-west-1 for 48h with synthetic SLO probes - If no regressions, progressive rollout to remaining regions over 72h - Rollback: disable feature flag or revert hotfix; immediate step: set routed_fraction max to 0 to disable broker if needed Performance impact: - Expected median p50 unchanged; tail latency p99 during drains reduced from ~2.6s to ~1.1s in simulation; SLO breaches predicted to drop by ~75% under same load profile. Rollback plan included in docs/operational/keystone.md Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2025-01-14 after approvals from reviewers. Post-merge actions: - Monitor keystone.leases.active and fallback.broker.routed_fraction dashboards - Run canary healthcheck automation every 2h during rollout - Follow up ENG ticket to consider making keystone part of Dedicated deployment flow (ENG-2209)
notes: Merge method: squash. Post-merge CI: green. Canary started: eu-west-1 2025-01-15 03:00 UTC.
rollback_instructions: Set feature flag runtime.enable_connection_keystone=false to immediately disable keystone and set fallback.max_routed_fraction=0 to stop broker routing; if that fails, revert hotfix commit on main and redeploy.
